description.p: ServeMedia is The Self-Hosted Media-Center for Linux. It is built around a core module called MatchMedia which acts as a statistical engine responsible for directory hierarchy discovery of media libraries, title extraction and grouping, metadata search-and-fetch from providers like TVMaze, statistically scoring and ranking candidates and mapping them to the appropriate files and folder hierarchies. ServeMedia is built to be lightweight, minimal and concise, yet feature-complete for a self hosted media center. ServeMedia can be both: a standalone desktop application with a desktop entry and a webkit wrapped gui on a single device, and a media server which can serve a server-side-rendered frontend over the local network. Compatible files play directly. Other files are transcoded to HLS, on the GPU when the driver check succeeds.

Title page with plot and seasons

ul.li: Subtitle tracks stay visible on first play. WebVTT conversion is one shared ffmpeg run per file, and the player no longer tears the track down while that request is still in flight. Fixes #3.
Recently added titles open the file or its folder. A file that sits in the library root no longer opens /libraries/1.
Episode titles keep a trailing parenthesis unless it is a resolution, codec, or bit depth.

li.em: Settings has a Networks tab. Save and Reset rebind the listen address immediately.

ul.li: The window remembers unmaximized, maximized, or big picture, and opens that way next time. The title-bar button maximizes at 700×1120. Leaving big picture restores the previous size. Links that leave the app open in the system browser.
Title, plot, and poster edits share one dialog. Breadcrumbs scroll as a ticker.

Changes scans write sidecars through MatchMedia 0.2.5, one folded show at a time, and keep a partial show NFO. A show is complete only when every season has its NFO and poster. Season NFOs include a premiere date. Seasons and episodes sort by title, premiere, date added, or episode number.
Home packs posters into square columns. Scroll position survives navigation. Posters enlarge on hover and open in a lightbox.

A container image is published as ghcr.io/alyshmahell/servemedia. It uses the host home, the four default library roots, and a watchdog timeout of 0. The documented run command starts it detached as servemedia.
Flatpak metadata lists the GitHub page and the donation link, and declares gamepad, touch, and a 360px minimum display.
